title: How to start selling on Amazon UK in 2026: the complete beginner's guide
description: Sell on Amazon.co.uk in 2026: £25/month plan, 2026 fee cuts and 2% surcharge, VAT for UK and overseas sellers, UKCA/GPSR, and your first 90 days.
tldr: Professional plan is £25/month excl. VAT; Individual is £0.75 per item, better under ~35 sales a month [s1].
Most referral fees are 8–15%; 2026 cuts took clothing to 5% up to £15 and home products to 8% up to £20 [s1][s3].
Low-Price FBA now covers most items at or below £20 [s1][s4]; a 2% fuel and logistics surcharge on FBA fees applies from 2 Nov 2026 [s1].
UK VAT threshold is £90,000, but overseas sellers (NETPs) must register from their first taxable sale [s13][s14].
Amazon accounts for VAT on overseas sellers' sales of goods already in the UK, and on imported consignments of £135 or less [s15].
From October 2027 Amazon is due to account for VAT on sales by UK businesses too, if they're VAT registered or sell over £90,000 a year on the platform [s16].
You need a GB EORI to import; the £135 customs duty relief ends by October 2028 at the latest [s17][s18].
Great Britain continues to recognise CE marking for most product types; EU GPSR applies to Northern Ireland sales [s19][s41][s20].
A UK trade mark costs £205 online (one class) and takes about 3 months; Brand Registry accepts a pending application [s27][s26][s28].

blocks.p: Amazon.co.uk is the UK's biggest online marketplace and one of Amazon's largest stores outside the US. It is a mature, competitive store: most everyday categories already have hundreds of sellers, and many of them are established brands or factory-direct sellers from overseas. That does not mean a beginner can't win. It means you win with a specific product, clean compliance and tight costs, not with luck.

Amazon does not publish an official count of active UK sellers or new UK sellers per year that we could verify for this guide, so we won't quote one. What we can say from Amazon's own 2026 announcements is where Amazon is pushing the store, and that tells you a lot about where the opportunity is.

blocks.h3: Amazon is cutting fees on cheap, everyday items

blocks.p: In 2026 Amazon made what it called one of its largest-ever European fee reductions: an average cut of £0.15 per unit across its European stores [s1][s3]. UK parcel fulfilment fees fell, referral fees dropped sharply in clothing, home and pet categories, and the cheaper **Low-Price FBA** rates were extended to most products priced at or below **£20** [s1][s3]. Read that as a signal: Amazon wants more low-priced, everyday products in the UK, and it is competing hard on price.

blocks.h3: But logistics costs are creeping back

blocks.p: At the same time, Amazon added a **fuel and logistics surcharge** on FBA fulfilment fees. It was 1.5% earlier in 2026 and rose to **2% from 2 November 2026** for the UK and nine EU stores [s1][s4]. A festive **peak fulfilment fee** also applies in Q4 [s5]. So the fee cuts are real, but your per-unit cost still moves during the year.

blocks.h3: AI shopping: from Rufus to Alexa for Shopping

blocks.p: Amazon launched its AI shopping assistant **Rufus** in the UK in 2024, first as a beta in the app and then for all UK customers on app and desktop [s30]. On **11 November 2026** Amazon launched **Alexa for Shopping** in the UK on the Amazon Shopping app and website, free for signed-in customers without needing Prime [s31][s32]. It can compare products on features and price and show up to a 365-day price history [s32].

For you, this means shoppers increasingly ask questions ("which water bottle stays cold all day and fits a car cup holder?") instead of typing two keywords. Listings that clearly answer real questions in the title, bullets, images and A+ content are easier for the assistant to recommend. Price history visibility also means fake "was" prices and spiky pricing will be more obvious to buyers.

callout.title: Low-price storefronts
callout.text: Amazon has tested a separate ultra-low-price storefront (Haul) in some countries. We could not confirm its UK status for this guide, so check Amazon's UK news page before planning around it. Either way, the £20 Low-Price FBA extension shows Amazon wants cheap everyday items in the main store.

blocks.p: Most new sellers on Amazon UK find that organic visibility in the first weeks depends heavily on paid ads. We could not find an official, current UK cost-per-click figure, so we won't quote one. Plan on ads being a real line in your budget, and use your own Amazon Ads console data (not blog averages) once you launch.

blocks.h3: What this means for a beginner

ul: **Good fit:** branded, light, small products in the £15–£40 range where you can improve on a weak point competitors share (read their 1–3 star reviews).
**Hard mode:** tiny-margin products under £10, electronics with heavy compliance, and categories dominated by big brands.
**Your edge:** being compliant (UKCA/CE, GPSR for Northern Ireland, EPR, VAT) when many overseas competitors cut corners, and writing listings that answer shopper questions for Alexa for Shopping.

sections.title: Is Amazon UK right for you?

ul: **UK residents and UK companies.** You can use the standard £90,000 VAT registration threshold [s13], get a GB EORI easily [s17], and receive payouts in GBP to a UK bank.
**Sellers who want a gateway to Europe.** Once you have UK stock and a brand, Amazon's Global Selling programme can help you list in EU stores [s39], though EU VAT and customs are separate.
**Brand builders with light, small products.** UK fees in 2026 favour small parcels and items under £20 [s1].
Sellers who need a very low price point and can't absorb a VAT charge (overseas sellers must register for VAT from the first sale on goods in the UK, see below) [s13].
Sellers of heavily regulated goods (electricals, toys, cosmetics, food) who don't yet have test reports and a UK/NI compliance plan.
Anyone hoping to start with no money for ads and inventory.

blocks.h3: If you're based outside the UK (India, China, US, EU…)

blocks.p: You can sell on Amazon.co.uk from abroad, but the rules change in three important ways:

ol: **VAT from day one.** If you're a non-established taxable person (NETP), meaning no UK business establishment, the £90,000 threshold does not apply. You must register for UK VAT if you make any taxable supplies in the UK, within 30 days of the first one or of expecting to make one [s13][s14].

**Who collects VAT on Amazon.** For goods already in the UK at the point of sale (for example in an FBA warehouse), Amazon as the online marketplace is treated as the supplier and accounts for the VAT on sales to UK consumers, whatever the value [s15]. For goods shipped from abroad in consignments of £135 or less, the marketplace also charges the VAT [s15][s14]. Even so, you usually still need a UK VAT number because importing stock into the UK is itself a VAT event, and HMRC says you can register for VAT to reclaim the import VAT you paid [s15]. (If all your UK sales go through a marketplace, HMRC's manual says you can ask for exemption from registration, because your deemed supply to the marketplace is zero-rated, but then you can't reclaim import VAT [s14].)

**Customs.** To import into Great Britain you need a GB EORI number, which usually requires UK premises; if you're not eligible, you appoint someone (such as a customs agent) to deal with customs for you [s17]. Each shipment needs a customs declaration and duty at the rate for your commodity code [s35].

blocks.p: Amazon pays UK sellers in GBP. If your bank is outside the UK, check the deposit options and currency conversion fees in Seller Central during sign-up. Compare the conversion rate Amazon offers with a regulated currency provider before you choose.

blocks.p: Amazon checks that you are who you say you are before you can sell. Expect document checks, and possibly a live video call with an Amazon representative where you show your ID, or an in-person or postcard address check. The exact steps vary by country and business type, so follow the prompts in Seller Central and use Seller University for walkthroughs [s38].

callout.title: Common reasons for delay or rejection
callout.text: Blurry or cropped documents; a name or address that doesn't match exactly across ID, statement and form; a statement older than Amazon accepts; using a card or bank account in someone else's name; opening a second account without approval. Fix these before you submit.

After approval, set up two-step verification and add users with their own logins, never shared passwords.

blocks.p: All Amazon fees below are as published or reported for 2026. Amazon changes fees often. Before you order stock, run your exact product through Amazon's **Revenue Calculator** [s40] and check the official FBA rate card [s4].

callout.title: Not tax advice
callout.text: UK VAT for marketplace sellers is genuinely complicated, especially if you're overseas or import stock. Use this to understand the rules, then confirm with an accountant who works with Amazon sellers.

blocks.p: **VAT (Value Added Tax)** is the UK's sales tax, included in the price shoppers see. HMRC runs it. The current registration threshold for UK-established businesses is **£90,000** of taxable turnover [s13][s36]. Below that you don't have to register (you can choose to). The standard rate is **20%**, with a 5% reduced rate and 0% for some goods [s42].

blocks.h3: Overseas sellers: register from the first sale

blocks.p: If you have no UK establishment, you're a **non-established taxable person (NETP)**. The threshold does not apply to NETPs: you must register if you make taxable supplies of any value in the UK, within 30 days of making (or expecting to make) one, and HMRC registers you from the date you became liable [s13]. If all your UK sales go through a marketplace, you can ask HMRC for exemption from registration [s14].

head: Situation

rows: Overseas seller, goods already in the UK (e.g. FBA stock), sold to a UK consumer

Amazon charges and accounts for the VAT [s15][s14]

You charge and pay VAT yourself once registered. From October 2027, Amazon is due to account for it if you're VAT registered or sell over £90,000 a year on the platform [s16]
table.note: The £135 test is per consignment, not per item [s15]. From October 2027 the government plans to extend marketplace VAT liability to UK businesses (not B2B, personal or second-hand sales) [s16].

blocks.p: Even when Amazon accounts for VAT on your sales, overseas sellers still import stock into the UK, which brings import VAT. HMRC says you can register for VAT to reclaim it [s15].

ul: **EORI:** you need a GB EORI number to import into England, Wales or Scotland. It usually requires UK premises; if you're not eligible, appoint someone to deal with customs for you. Northern Ireland moves may also need an XI EORI [s17].
**Duty:** each import needs a customs declaration and duty based on the commodity code of your product [s35]. Most sellers use a freight forwarder or customs agent.

**Low-value relief is ending:** the £135 customs duty relief for low-value imports will be removed by October 2028 at the latest, with new customs arrangements, including a UK fiscal representative for overseas sellers [s18]. This mostly affects sellers shipping individual parcels from abroad, not bulk FBA imports.

blocks.p: UK residents pay income tax (sole traders) or corporation tax (companies) on profit, not revenue. Keep every Amazon settlement report, supplier invoice and shipping bill. Overseas sellers are usually taxed on profits at home, but check your own country's rules and any tax treaty.

ul: Before your first import if you're overseas (VAT and EORI setup).
When you approach the £90,000 threshold as a UK seller [s13].
Before you expand to EU stores, which brings EU VAT.

sections.title: Product compliance, safety and brand protection

blocks.p: Some categories and products need approval before you can list ("gated"), and some are restricted or banned. In Seller Central, search a product in "Add a product" to see if it needs approval. Expect extra checks for things like toys, cosmetics, food, electricals and medical-type products.

For Great Britain (England, Scotland, Wales), legislation in force since 1 October 2024 continues to recognise **CE marking** for most product rules, so you can use UKCA or CE [s19][s41]. Some sectors have their own rules, including cableways, construction products, marine equipment, medical devices, rail products, transportable pressure equipment and drones [s19]. For example, CE-marked medical devices are recognised in GB until July 2028 or 2030, depending on the EU legislation they meet [s41]. UKCA can be placed on a label or accompanying document until 31 December 2027 [s19].

blocks.h3: GPSR: Great Britain vs Northern Ireland

ul: **Great Britain:** consumer products stay under the UK General Product Safety Regulations 2005 [s20].

**Northern Ireland:** the EU General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) has applied to consumer products placed on the NI market since 13 December 2024 [s20]. You need a **responsible economic operator** (a business in the EU or NI that holds the product safety information and is the contact for regulators) [s20].
Because Amazon.co.uk delivers to Northern Ireland, check whether your listings can ship there and whether you have a responsible person set up.

blocks.p: Your product and packaging should show who made it and who is responsible for it, in English, with any required warnings and markings. Keep test reports and a technical file ready: Amazon and Trading Standards can ask for them. Under the Product Regulation and Metrology Act 2025, the government can require more marking, warnings and recalls, and has consulted on a new product safety framework with clearer responsibilities across the supply chain [s21][s22].
**Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)** makes businesses pay for the packaging they put on the UK market. Thresholds use turnover and tonnes of packaging [s23]:

head: Your business
Status
rows: Turnover £1m+ and over 25 tonnes of packaging
£1m–£2m turnover with over 25 tonnes, or over £2m with 25–50 tonnes
Under 25 tonnes, or turnover £1m or less
table.note: Applies to UK-established businesses, with group totals counted; Amazon, as an online marketplace, is covered for packaging supplied from outside the UK [s23]. Small producer registration for the 2027 reporting year: £1,303 direct with the regulator or £696 through a compliance scheme, by 1 April 2027 [s24]. Most beginners will be below the thresholds, but check every year.

blocks.p: If you sell electrical or electronic equipment, WEEE rules apply. Since 12 August 2025, marketplaces are treated as producers for electrical goods sold by non-UK sellers to UK households [s25]. UK-based sellers of electricals have their own producer and take-back duties; read the current rules before you list.

**Brand Registry** is Amazon's free programme that gives you control over your brand's listings, A+ content, Brand Store, Sponsored Brands ads and IP-reporting tools. You need a pending or registered trade mark from the trade mark office of a country with an Amazon store, such as the UK IPO [s28].

head: UKIPO step
Typical time
rows: Publication in the trade marks journal (if no objections)
2 weeks after publication ends; around 3 months in total (the IPO also says 3 to 4 months) [s26][s27]
table.note: Fees: £205 online for one class, plus £60 per extra class [s27].

blocks.p: **IP Accelerator** connects you with vetted IP law firms. Amazon doesn't charge for the introduction (you pay the firm; Amazon lists a maximum provider fee of £240 for filing a UK application), and you get a broader range of brand protection benefits sooner while your trade mark is still pending [s29].

sections.title: Choosing your first product with data

ul: Sells for roughly £15–£40, so fees and ads don't eat the margin.
Small and light, ideally a small parcel under 1 kg (see the FBA table) [s4].
Not gated, not electrical, not a toy for under-14s, not a cosmetic or food, unless you already know those rules.
Steady demand all year, not just Christmas.
Competitors have clear, fixable complaints in their reviews.
You can add something real: better materials, a bundle, a size competitors don't offer.

blocks.p: A simple rule many sellers use: aim for your **landed cost (product + shipping + duty) to be no more than about a quarter to a third of your selling price**, so Amazon fees, ads and VAT still leave profit. Using our example: on a £24.99 item, Amazon fees were £6.81 [s1][s4]. If your landed cost is £6 and you spend £3 per unit on ads, you have about £9 left before VAT and storage. If you're VAT registered, take VAT out first. That's thin but workable; a £12 landed cost would not be.

blocks.h3: Validate demand with Amazon's own tools

ul: **Product Opportunity Explorer** (in Seller Central): search volume, growth and return rates for customer needs.
**Brand Analytics** (after Brand Registry): top search terms and what shoppers click.
**Revenue Calculator**: your exact fees before you buy stock [s40].
**Amazon search itself**: read the top 10 listings, their reviews and questions, and notice what Alexa for Shopping highlights when you ask about the product [s31].
**Seasonal:** Christmas-only or summer-only products (standard-size storage roughly doubles in Oct–Dec [s1]).
**Fragile:** glass and ceramics get damaged and returned.
**Gated or regulated:** needs approvals or test reports.
**Patented or branded designs:** copying a design invites IP complaints.
**Heavy or oversize:** expensive fulfilment and storage.
**Under £10:** even with Low-Price FBA, ads can wipe out the margin.

blocks.p: For most first products, **FBA** is the easier choice. The Prime badge usually helps conversion, and you don't have to handle daily shipping. Use the Revenue Calculator to compare FBA and your own shipping costs [s40].

blocks.h3: Europe: EFN, Pan-EU and Remote Fulfilment

blocks.p: Since Brexit, moving stock between the UK and the EU is an import/export with customs and VAT on both sides. Amazon has programmes for cross-border selling, such as the **European Fulfilment Network (EFN)** for fulfilling orders in other stores from one country's stock, and **Pan-European FBA** for EU stores [s4]. Check Global Selling for which programmes currently link the UK and the EU [s39], and get VAT advice first.

head: When
What to do

Ship stock in. While it's travelling, apply for Brand Registry (trade mark filed via IP Accelerator if needed [s29]).

ul: **Day 30:** listing live, stock received, ads running, first sales, first Vine reviews coming in.
**Day 60:** daily sales stable, a handful of genuine reviews, ACoS falling week by week, first reorder placed.
**Day 90:** profitable or close to it after ads, rating of 4 stars or more, and a clear list of the search terms that make you money.

callout.title: Use Seller University
callout.text: Amazon's free Seller University has UK-specific videos for listings, FBA shipments and ads [s38]. Watch the module before each step.

ul: **Sponsored Products:** ads for single products in search results and product pages. Start here.
**Sponsored Brands:** banner-style ads with your logo and several products (needs Brand Registry).
**Sponsored Display:** ads that re-target shoppers and appear on and off Amazon.
**ACoS (Advertising Cost of Sale):** ad spend ÷ ad sales. £20 spend for £100 of ad sales = 20% ACoS.
**TACoS (Total ACoS):** ad spend ÷ all sales (ads + organic). It shows if ads are building organic sales.
**Negative keyword:** a search term you block so you stop paying for useless clicks.

ol: One **automatic** Sponsored Products campaign to discover search terms.
One **manual exact** campaign with 5–15 of your best keywords.
One **manual phrase** or broad campaign to find new terms.
Later, one **Sponsored Brands** campaign once you're brand registered.

blocks.p: Starter budget: decide what you can afford to lose while learning (our example budget used £10–£15 a day). We couldn't find a credible current UK cost-per-click average, so watch your own costs in the Amazon Ads console for the first two weeks before scaling.

In launch, ACoS above your profit margin is normal because you're buying data and reviews. After 6–8 weeks, aim for ACoS at or below your margin before ads, and a TACoS that falls as organic sales rise.

faq.q: Is it still worth selling on Amazon UK in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, if you pick a specific, light product priced around £15–£40 and do compliance properly. Amazon cut many fees for items under £20 in 2026, but a 2% fuel and logistics surcharge and Q4 peak fees still apply. It's competitive, so budget for ads.

faq.q: How much does it cost to start selling on Amazon UK?
faq.a: The Professional plan is £25 a month excluding VAT, or Individual is £0.75 per item sold. On top of that you pay referral fees (mostly 8–15%), FBA fees, storage and ads. A realistic first private-label launch often needs a few thousand pounds including stock.

faq.q: Do I need to be VAT registered to sell on Amazon UK?
faq.a: UK-based sellers only have to register once taxable turnover passes £90,000. Overseas sellers with no UK establishment must register from their first taxable sale in the UK. Amazon accounts for VAT on many overseas sellers' sales, and from October 2027 on VAT-registered UK sellers' sales too.

faq.q: Can I sell on Amazon UK from India or China?
faq.a: Yes. You'll need UK VAT registration from day one, a GB EORI number for imports, and a customs agent. Amazon accounts for VAT on sales of goods already in the UK, but you handle import VAT and duty.
Individual suits fewer than about 35 sales a month. Professional is £25 a month and unlocks ads, Brand Registry tools and bulk listing, so most serious sellers choose it.

faq.q: How long does a UK trade mark take for Brand Registry?
faq.a: Around 3 months if nobody objects (the IPO says 3 to 4 months). Brand Registry accepts a pending application, and IP Accelerator unlocks more protection benefits while it's pending. The online fee is £205 for one class.

faq.q: Do I need UKCA or is CE fine?
faq.a: For most product types sold in Great Britain, CE marking continues to be recognised, and UKCA is also fine. Medical devices, construction products and a few other sectors have their own rules.

faq.q: What is GPSR and does it apply to UK sellers?
faq.a: GPSR is the EU General Product Safety Regulation. It applies to consumer products sold into Northern Ireland since 13 December 2024, but not to Great Britain. If you ship to NI, you need an EU or NI responsible operator.

faq.q: What are FBA fees in the UK?
faq.a: They depend on size and weight. Amazon's rate card (effective 2 November 2026) puts a 400 g small parcel at £3.00 before the 2% surcharge. Use Amazon's Revenue Calculator for your exact product.

faq.q: Why did my FBA fees go up in November?
faq.a: Amazon raised its fuel and logistics surcharge from 1.5% to 2% of fulfilment fees on 2 November 2026, and peak fulfilment fees run from mid-October to mid-January.

faq.q: Do I need to worry about packaging EPR?
faq.a: Most beginners don't have full obligations. They start at £1 million turnover and more than 25 tonnes of packaging a year, with group totals counted. Check again every year as you grow.

faq.q: What gets new Amazon UK accounts suspended?
faq.a: Mismatched verification documents, a second account without approval, fake or incentivised reviews, IP complaints from copying brands, and inauthentic-item complaints you can't answer with invoices.
It's Amazon's AI shopping assistant, which launched in the UK on 11 November 2026 and builds on Rufus. It compares products and shows price history, so clear, question-answering listings matter more.
